findings.text: Per-VCPU control dispatcher handles debug registers, extended save areas in two sizes, extended control registers, TSC rate query and update, pvclock pause notification, generic capability enable, nested state save and restore, optional Hyper-V and Xen attributes, special registers version two, generic device attributes and memory encryption. Unknown requests fail as invalid and every path releases a temporary buffer and the VCPU reference.

Legacy extended save retrieval is refused when the guest FPU user size exceeds the legacy container size. Variable sized retrieval and update use the current guest FPU user size for host allocation and user transfer, with allocation failure, helper failure and user copy failure propagated distinctly.

TSC rate update is refused when the guest TSC is protected and when platform TSC control exists and the requested rate reaches the platform maximum. A zero request selects the host TSC rate. Retrieval returns the stored virtual rate. Pause notification delegates to a guest-paused helper.

Nested state save and restore are gated on nested support. Save reads the caller supplied buffer length, invokes a vendor get operation, returns success when the result fits, and otherwise writes back the required length and reports too big. Restore checks header length, restricts flags to a small allowed set where run pending requires guest mode, and invokes a vendor set operation under SRCU protection.

Special register set two in both directions is refused when the VM supports protected state and the VCPU is in protected state. Retrieval allocates a host object, fills it through a helper, then copies out. Update duplicates the user object and then calls a validation helper. Device attributes delegate to a common handler. Memory encryption requires a vendor hook and otherwise reports not a typewriter.

Xen per-VCPU attribute update accepts VCPU info by guest address or host address, VCPU time info, runstate mapping, runstate current value, full runstate data, runstate adjustment, VCPU identifier, timer configuration and upcall vector. Unknown types keep a not-found result.

VCPU info and time info use a guest mapping cache. A sentinel guest address or a zero host address deactivates the cache and succeeds. Otherwise the cache is activated for the size of the corresponding shared structure and a clock update request is queued on success.

Runstate mapping requires scheduler statistics support. A sentinel address deactivates primary and overflow caches. Otherwise the needed size depends on address width and Xen long mode, the first cache covers the remainder of the first page, a second cache covers any spill onto the next page, failure deactivates both, and success refreshes the guest view.

Runstate current, data and adjust all require scheduler statistics. Current only checks the state range. Data checks range, requires the entry time to equal the sum of running plus runnable plus blocked plus offline time, and requires the VM clock to have reached the entry time before storing state, entry time, counters and steal baseline. Adjust allows a no-change sentinel for state, checks the same sum and monotonicity against old plus delta values, accumulates the deltas, and then either changes state or refreshes the guest mapping when active.

VCPU identifier must be below the architectural VCPU maximum. Timer update requires two-level priority whenever a port is set, stops any running timer before changing the vector, stores the new port, and arms the timer only when both port and expiry are nonzero. Upcall vector accepts zero or values at or above sixteen.

Xen per-VCPU attribute query returns the stored mapping addresses or sentinels, runstate address and values, identifier, timer snapshot and upcall vector. Runstate queries require scheduler statistics. Adjustment query is write only and always fails as invalid. Unmapped runstate address keeps a not-found result.

VCPU info query distinguishes guest-address backed and host-address backed activation and reports invalid guest sentinel or zero host value when inactive. Time info reports invalid sentinel when inactive. Runstate data reports current state plus entry time plus four counters. Identifier and upcall vector return stored values directly.

Timer query produces a consistent migration snapshot by cancelling the high resolution timer and injecting pending timer interrupts when an expiry is armed, sampling port plus fixed two-level priority plus expiry, then rearming the timer from its expiry when still armed. Duplicate delivery after migration is treated as idempotent.

Host-address activation of a guest mapping cache validates the caller user range first and fails as invalid when inaccessible, otherwise forwards to a common activation path with a marker guest address.

Guest-address active means the cache is active and its guest address is not an error address. Host-address active means the cache is active and its guest address is an error address. The two predicates are mutually exclusive when active.
VCPU page fault handling for the architecture always reports a bus error and maps nothing.
Triple-state segment base update rejects addresses within three pages of the top of the 32 bit range, otherwise delegates to a vendor hook. Identity map update delegates directly to a vendor hook.
Requested MMU page count below a minimum is refused. Otherwise the change and the stored requested count are performed while holding the slot mutex.
Dirty log synchronization does nothing when per-CPU dirty buffering is disabled. Otherwise it kicks every VCPU so that buffered entries are flushed through an exit before userspace reads the bitmap.

VM capability enable requires zero flags and dispatches on capability id including quirk control, split IRQ chip, x2APIC API, exit suppression, platform info, exception payload, triple fault event, userspace MSR interception, bus lock behavior, SGX attributes, encrypted context copy and move, hypercall exit, emulation failure exit, PMU capability, maximum VCPU id and notify exit.

Extended quirk disable validates the mask against supported quirks, then both quirk forms OR the supported bits into stored disabled quirks under the VM lock. Split IRQ chip requires a reserved pin count within the route limit, no in-kernel chip and no created VCPUs, then records split mode and reserved pins with an ordering barrier and clears the absent APIC virtualization inhibit.

x2APIC API validates flag subset, forbids enabling and disabling broadcast suppression together, requires split IRQ mode for enabling suppression, and then records 32 bit id format, broadcast quirk disable and suppression mode. Exit suppression validates against the allowed mask, requires no created VCPUs, emits a one-time cross-thread return prediction warning when mitigation is off and broader exits are suppressed on a vulnerable SMT-capable CPU, then applies the mask.

Several capabilities store the first argument directly after optional mask checks: platform info readability, exception payload, triple fault event, userspace MSR mask, hypercall exit mask, and a zero-or-one emulation failure mode. Bus lock mode validates the mask, forbids off plus exit together, and enables exit only when hardware supports it.

SGX attribute enable resolves allowed attributes through a helper and only permits the provisioning key attribute alone. Encrypted context copy and move require the corresponding vendor hook. PMU capability requires global PMU enable and a valid mask, restricts protected PMU to disable, requires no created VCPUs and no mediated PMU, and stores enable as the negation of disable. Maximum VCPU id requires a value within the id limit and records it once while respecting the boot CPU id. Notify exit validates 32 bit mask bits, requires hardware support and the enabled bit, and requires no created VCPUs.

Xen attribute update holds the Xen mutex across the whole switch and also holds an SRCU read section, releasing SRCU before the mutex. Xen query holds only the Xen mutex. Nested state restore holds an SRCU read section around the vendor set call. MMU page count holds the slot mutex. Quirk, split chip, exit suppression, PMU and maximum id paths hold the VM lock.

User memory failures surface as fault errors, allocation failures as out of memory, unsupported or malformed requests as invalid, oversized nested retrieval as too big with required length written back, missing vendor hooks as not-a-typewriter or invalid, missing scheduler statistics as operation not supported, and unknown Xen types as not found.

A reserved invalid guest address sentinel means no Xen mapping and selects deactivation. A zero host address has the same no-mapping meaning for host-backed VCPU info. Upcall vectors below sixteen are invalid except zero which clears the vector. VCPU identifiers are bounded by the architectural VCPU maximum.

Runstate size selection follows guest address width and Xen long mode, with mapping split at the end of the containing page and an overflow mapping for any remainder. MMU page requests have a documented minimum. TSS base must leave room for three pages below the top of the address range.

The VCPU interface exchanges fixed host-sized objects for debug registers, extended save area, extended control registers, capability enable, nested state header and special registers version two. Xen exchanges a tagged union carrying guest address, host address, runstate tuple, timer tuple, identifier or vector.

Runstate data is a state value plus entry timestamp plus four cumulative counters for running, runnable, blocked and offline. Timer state is a port plus priority plus absolute expiry in nanoseconds. Mapping caches expose active state plus guest address plus user address used by the active-kind predicates.
